Question: Which statement about cycloalkanes is incorrect?

Options:
A. Any disubstituted cycloalkane can have cis-trans isomers
B. Cyclopentane is nonplanar to avoid the torsional strain between adjacent C-H bonds
C. The least strained form of any unsubstituted cycloalkane is the chair conformation of cyclohexane
D. The planar form of any cycloalkane with a ring larger than cyclopropane will not be the most stable conformation

Thought: I need to analyze each statement about cycloalkanes and determine which one is incorrect.

A. "Any disubstituted cycloalkane can have cis-trans isomers" - Let me think about this. For a disubstituted cycloalkane to have cis-trans isomers, the two substituents need to be on different carbon atoms. If they're on the same carbon, there can't be cis-trans isomerism. So not "any" disubstituted cycloalkane can have cis-trans isomers. This statement seems incorrect.

B. "Cyclopentane is nonplanar to avoid the torsional strain between adjacent C-H bonds" - Cyclopentane does adopt a nonplanar conformation (envelope or half-chair) to minimize torsional strain. This statement is correct.

C. "The least strained form of any unsubstituted cycloalkane is the chair conformation of cyclohexane" - This statement is comparing all cycloalkanes and claiming that the chair conformation of cyclohexane has the least strain among all cycloalkanes. This is correct - cyclohexane in the chair conformation has minimal angle strain and torsional strain compared to other cycloalkanes.

D. "The planar form of any cycloalkane with a ring larger than cyclopropane will not be the most stable conformation" - This is correct. Cyclopropane is planar due to its geometry, but larger cycloalkanes adopt non-planar conformations to minimize strain.

After analyzing all statements, it appears that statement A is incorrect because not all disubstituted cycloalkanes can have cis-trans isomers - specifically, if both substituents are on the same carbon atom, cis-trans isomerism is not possible.
Final Answer: [ANSWER]A[/ANSWER]
